title: Finite witnesses and the width hierarchy for language generation
abstract: Characterizes generation in the limit for arbitrary families of infinite languages over any countably infinite universe by finite positive witnesses. Ordered-history generators admit a single set-driven normalization, chosen before the target language. The separation-width invariant takes every value 0, 1, 2, ..., omega, omega+1; generation is equivalent to width at most omega. Reusable infrastructure includes locking witnesses, positive separation, bounded diagonal capture over arbitrary universes, transport under equivalences, and finite-query normalization on natural numbers. The formalized scope is the semantic characterization and hierarchy, not the paper's additional density-one or Turing-computability results in Appendices D and E.

informal.GenLimit.FiniteWitness.Simplified.ordina: For any family H of infinite languages over a countably infinite universe, there exists one ordered-history generator that eventually outputs an unseen target element on every exact presentation of every target in H if and only if H admits a finite positive witness assignment whose nonempty active subfamilies always have infinite common intersection.
informal.GenLimit.FiniteWitness.Simplified.univer: Every ordered-history generator over a countably infinite universe has one set-driven normalization that locks on every infinite target on which the original generator succeeds on all exact presentations. The normalization is chosen before the target.
informal.GenLimit.FiniteWitness.ordinary_iff_widt: A family of infinite languages over a countably infinite universe is generatable in the limit exactly when its separation width is at most omega.
informal.GenLimit.FiniteWitness.full_range: Over every countably infinite universe, every value in WithTop (WithTop Nat), representing 0, 1, 2, ..., omega, omega+1, is the separation width of some family of infinite languages.
informal.GenLimit.FiniteWitness.bounded_capture: Over an arbitrary universe, every sequence of uniformly bounded finite sets has infinitely many terms contained in one set D such that D contains none of a prescribed countable list of infinite cores.
informal.GenLimit.FiniteWitness.executable_univer: The finite-search normalization on natural numbers locks on every infinite language on which the supplied generator eventually succeeds on every exact presentation. This is a semantic correctness theorem for the defined procedure, without a formal Turing-computability claim.
